A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BioCAP study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and retrieval experiments, training ablations, qualitative analyses, and a human caption evaluation in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds caption-generator comparisons, localization evaluation, annotation validation, subgroup analyses, and few-shot and biological visual-task results.

M1.justification: The proposed method retains shared encoders, separate taxonomy/caption visual projectors, joint label-and-caption supervision, and Wikipedia-guided caption generation with taxonomic format examples. Expanded curation and genus-fallback descriptions document existing steps. Alternative caption generators are tested without changing the adopted InternVL3 38B pipeline.

E1.justification: v3 adds CUB localization evaluation and evaluations on FishNet, NeWT, AwA2, and Herbarium 2019 in Tables 14 and 19. These substantially broaden evaluated data and task coverage beyond the retained classification and retrieval benchmarks. Appendix G discusses other scientific domains without experimentally evaluating them.

E2.justification: The main classification and retrieval comparator sets remain unchanged. New Tables 18–19 add Supervised-IN21K and quantitative comparisons with DINOv3, which previously appeared in embedding visualizations. Table 7 also evaluates Qwen2.5-VL 32B and LLaVA-NeXT 34B as alternative caption generators.

E3.justification: New Appendix D.3 reports overlap filtering, while retrieval-set sizes change from 7,007 to 7,000 Cornell Bird pairs and 2,349 to 2,254 PlantID pairs. Added protocols include one-/five-shot evaluation, bounding-box localization using the energy-based pointing game, and stratification by Wikipedia coverage and the bottom 5% of training-image counts. Existing main training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's prompt, projector, and training-component ablations, v3 tests exemplar count, taxonomic level, independent exemplar generation, and captioner family/size. It adds quantitative localization, Gemini/human verification of behavior labels, underrepresented-species analysis, genus-fallback examples, and caption-quality ablations for few-shot classification. These examine several previously untested design choices and reliability questions.

E5.justification: Tables 18–20 introduce ± reporting for model performance, and Appendix E.3 explicitly describes two independently generated exemplar sets with retraining. However, the meaning of ±, associated run counts, and seeds are unspecified. The existing human-evaluation agreement statistics remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Retrieval values change throughout Tables 2–3; BioCAP's Table 2 mean changes from 52.6 to 53.5 under revised evaluation sets, not an established same-setting gain. Substantial new results include localization scores of 0.47 versus BioCLIP's 0.43 and small average few-shot/visual-task advantages in Tables 18–19. Table 1 remains unchanged. New Table 17 inconsistently reports Rare Species scores of 46.4/37.6 for BioCAP/BioCLIP versus 44.2/37.1 in Table 1.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A retain the same latent-trait/noise assumptions, InfoNCE analysis, and covariance decomposition. No substantive mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: domain-guided synthetic captions provide complementary supervision and improve biological semantic understanding, classification, and retrieval. Added experiments support and qualify these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1's explicit limitation about untested captioner dependence and adds robustness interpretations from generator comparisons. Appendix E.5 proposes that captions enrich within-species semantics without substantially improving between-species separation, explaining limited few-shot gains. Appendix B.4 adds biological reasoning for genus fallback, while Appendix G proposes conditions for applicability beyond biodiversity.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies two format-example curators, acceptance criteria, and disagreement resolution. Appendix D.3 documents perceptual hashing with distance threshold 10. Existing generation prompts, hardware, training hyperparameters, and code/data access statements are retained; these additions primarily improve procedural documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for alternative caption generators, new benchmarks, localization evaluation, perceptual hashing, and the biological rationale for genus fallback. Appendix G broadens scientific-domain positioning, but Section 2 and Appendix F largely retain the original relationship to biological foundation models and general synthetic-caption methods.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction and related-work edits, expanded curation explanations, additional appendix subsections, and updated affiliations and conference headers. The limitations appendix is removed and broader-applicability discussion added. The main section sequence and most existing prose, including the abstract and conclusion, remain stable.

P2.justification: Substantial new displays include Tables 6–7, 11, and 14–20 for ablations, annotation agreement, localization, subgroup results, and few-shot/visual-task comparisons, plus Figure 8's genus-fallback examples. Existing main figures are redistributed across pages, and earlier appendix figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical credibility by reporting removal of detected training–retrieval overlap, testing the captioner dependence explicitly left unresolved in v1, validating automatic behavior labels, and supplementing qualitative localization with quantitative evidence. The added few-shot analyses also clarify limits of caption supervision. Undefined ± statistics and inconsistent Rare Species values in Table 17 weaken parts of the new reporting, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and understanding of applicability.
